messages:
anya: Kicking off onboarding intake for argo-20b (community checkpoint) — wanted to drop a perf/quantization plan here. Requester: product-proto team. Priority: medium, but could bump to high if latency wins out.

park: SGTM. First step: baseline FP16 perf + int8 quant smoke. Can we do quick throughput vs p50 latency sweep at 2k/8k ctx?

sasha: I can run batch-size sweep. Proposed config: batch sizes [1,2,4,8], auto-batching off to measure single-request p50, then on to see throughput. Also include continous-batch mode to mimic muxed traffic.

devon: For ctx sweep, let's do [2k, 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k]. Important to measure kv-cache population overhead and first-token cost. Also capture peak memory at each ctx for int8/FP16.

anya: +1. Also need quality regression checks (toxicity, instruction-following) against our standard eval sets before we promote int8. Sasha — can you coordinate with QA for eval vectors?

sasha: Yup, will spin up eval job. Quick note: argo-20b uses grouped-gemm layers; quant toolchain needs per-channel calibration, not naive symmetric. I'll test both per-tensor and per-channel int8 to compare perf/quality.

park: ml-bench-bot — can you run a fast smoke bench (10k tokens) with default serving stack on a g5.12xlarge equivalent and post results? Command we want is:
```
rbench run --model argo-20b --variant fp16,int8-perchannel --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8 --ctx 2048 --duration 300s --out json
```

ml-bench-bot: Quick smoke queued. Will post raw numbers when done.

ml-bench-bot: Done. Summary (g5.12x equiv):
- FP16 single request p50: 85ms, p95: 150ms, tokens/s (batch=8): 4600
- int8-perchannel single req p50: 110ms, p95: 210ms, tokens/s (batch=8): 7300
- mem FP16: 42GB, int8-perchannel: 28GB
- cold start overhead FP16 ~380ms, int8 ~460ms
(raw: /mnt/bench/2112345678/argo20b-smoke.json)

anya: Interesting — int8 gives throughput up but p50 increases. We should check whether p50 for small batches (1) regresses in user-facing flows.

devon: Agree. Let's capture breakdown: token-gen time vs kernel-launch overhead. Run microbench for single-token latency with --trace to see GPU kernel times.

sasha: Running microbench now. Config: `rbench micro --model argo-20b --quant int8-perchannel --batch 1 --ctx 2048 --trace`

ml-bench-bot: Microbench trace summary: kernel compute dominates at high ctx fill; kernel-launch overhead ~4.5ms per step; token compute ~1.9ms per token on average for int8 at 2k ctx.

park: That kernel-launch overhead explains p50 shift. Could be due to additional dequant/depack steps in our runtime when using per-channel quant. We should test a fused path (dequant fused with attention) if available.

anya: Action items so far: [sasha] full batch/ctx sweep for FP16 + int8 (per-tensor + per-channel), capture p50/p95/tokens_s and memory; [devon] microbench traces and kernel breakdown; [park] runtime team follow-up on fused kernel paths; [anya] run quality evals against standard suites and flag regressions.

sasha: I'll aim to run sweep in the next 6 hours. If any result shows >20% p50 regression for batch=1 on int8-perchannel vs FP16, hold promotion and escalate.

devon: Note for velocity: also run a canary deploy with fallback policy in routing so we can route 10% traffic to int8 variant and auto-failover to fp16 on errors. Config snippet: 
```
rollout:
  variant: int8-perchannel
  traffic: 0.1
  fallback: fp16
  max_errors: 3
```

park: For reporting, let's produce a single perf sheet with columns: quant-mode, batch, ctx, p50, p95, tok/s, mem, cold-start, notes. Keep it lightweight.

anya: Sounds good. If QA passes and batch=1 p50 is within 15% we can consider a gradual rollout. Otherwise keep int8 for throughput-only routes.

ml-bench-bot: Noted. I'll attach full JSON outputs to the bench artefacts bucket. Path: s3://redwood-ml-bench/argo20b/2112345678/*.json

park: Thanks team. Sasha — ping when sweep finishes and we'll triage next steps for quant profile tuning. :thumbsup:
